study: E-T workload lower bound -> execution time -> slack, retained-data analysis, zero new performance launches

verdicts.lb_status: strict workload lower bound retained unconditionally (mathematical; independent of the time model)
verdicts.exit_condition: errors and applicability quantified; uncertainty reported as-is; no experiments added to chase significance

conclusions: Workload lower bound LB=max(sum w_e/8, max w_e) in PADDED-TOKEN units is strict (mathematical) and retained unconditionally; greedy base lands within 48-496 padded tokens (6.5-67.2 us converted) of LB.
Linear-compute assumption is supported at component level: expert gather = 339.3us + 0.1474us/padded-row, R2=0.976.
Fixed-communication assumption is REFUTED: dispatch+combine varies across layouts within a capture by 20-61x the within-layout repeat variance.

End-to-end single-slope conversion T=F+c*W has systematic role-dependent out-of-sample bias (+2-3% identity, +4-10% balanced; all role CIs exclude zero) -> per pre-frozen rule the time outputs are named BALANCED EXECUTION REFERENCE, not a strict time bound.
Gain prediction q_hat=c*deltaW is conservative: underestimates observed gains by 14.5-99.3us (2-11%); 5/8 per-capture error CIs compatible with zero, 3/8 exclude zero negative.

Remaining slack: identity layouts sit 632-903us above the converted LB reference; balanced layouts sit -109 to +4us around it, i.e. greedy balancing exhausts essentially all workload-LB headroom up to the conversion bias (~115us scale).
Exit condition met: explicit errors and applicability scope quantified; no further experiments added to chase a tighter actual-time upper bound.
invariants_reaffirmed: no new synthetic hidden states/routes/outputs/weights: all data are retained real captures and replays
no timing-based selection; triple layouts and capture roles pre-designated in the frozen spec
negatives preserved; zero-crossing CIs read as compatible-with-zero
no overhead subtraction from measured contrasts
